checks.rule: General-boundary registration is sufficient for most titles; extra precision requires a boundary agreement or determined-boundary process.
A determined boundary records the exact line for register purposes rather than merely a general boundary.
Do not treat HM Land Registry as resolving a disputed exact line; the exact line must already be identified before determination.
Surveying a determined boundary may use measurements from permanent features or Ordnance Survey National Grid coordinates.
A determined-boundary plan must identify start, end and turning points and describe the line claimed.
A determined-boundary plan must show sufficient surrounding detail and orientation such as a north point.
Preferred determined-boundary plan scale is no smaller than 1:200.
Reject a precision claim where the lodged plan carries a disclaimer casting doubt on its accuracy.
Measurement-based determined-boundary plans require measurements accurate to plus or minus 10 mm.
Boundary measurements must be horizontal rather than measured along a slope.
Measurements should be taken from at least two defined points on permanent physical features.
National Grid coordinates require plus or minus 300 mm absolute accuracy and plus or minus 10 mm relative accuracy.
